track.why: 15 Sep 2022, summited; the track and its waypoints (register box, creek crossing, left gully) follow the West Face approach, and the report's chockstone first pitch, ledge traverse and balancy summit slab with a rusty bolt are this route's pitches. facts.text: From the hairpin a short slide-alder bushwhack starts at a cairn and reaches a signed register box; the climbers' trail then follows the valley until the open talus and scree, where you cut left. Early Winters Creek was an easy crossing in mid-September, and the gully below the peak starts near 6,000 ft with open scree up to a cliff band, where you traverse left over a ridge.
Stash packs at the chockstone and climb the three short pitches light; pitch 1 passes behind the chockstone to a rappel anchor, and rapping from the top of it returns you to your packs.
The anchors below the summit block are poor: a loose flake and a slung boulder too small to trust. Build the belay from cams in the foot-level crack.
The summit slab must be dry. After mid-September rain one party waited for sun and would have turned back if it stayed wet.
Small cams (0.3 to 0.75) for the short pitches; a rap ring and webbing to replace the worn first anchor (July)
Do not lower or rappel from the rusty summit bolt; the leader down-climbs on a belay from the block anchor below. Linking the second and third pitches is a reasonable option.

notes: Only West Face has a trailhead pin; the other routes carry just a summit pin (the south-face routes would share the hairpin trailhead at 48.51454,-120.64332 but I did not propose adds because no track climbs them). Track 2028948 does the West Face, not Beckey-Tate, despite both sharing the summit slab; its start (48.51428,-120.64256) is 63 m from the pin, so no trailhead move. Our summit pin equals the surveyed Peakbagger coordinate; the track's highest point is 32 m away, so no summit move.
